events.summary: In the deep past, the Pthumerian civilization (and deeper ancient peoples) developed its own blood rituals and relationship with the Great Ones, later connected to the Chalice Dungeons.

Queen Yharnam, a Thumanrian queen, entered a contract with the formless Great One Oedon and bore his child Mergo, an act that effectively ended her existence and left her a suspended remnant; the Shadows of Yharnam served her.
Cainhurst Castle, predating the Healing Church, became the seat of an aristocratic family practicing their own blood arts known as the Vile Bloods.

Scholars of Byrgenwerth, including Willem and Laurence, discovered Ebrietas in the ancient Thumerian Labyrinths and uncovered buried Pthumerian knowledge of old blood and Great Ones, largely ignoring its implications.
Ebrietas, a Great One from the space between stars, shared her purer cosmic blood with Byrgenwerth's scholars for their research.
A traitor from Byrgenwerth brought forbidden blood knowledge to Cainhurst, allowing the Vile Bloods to refine their arts.

Laurence left Byrgenwerth against Willem's warnings, took the old blood, and founded the Healing Church, which genuinely and effectively practiced blood ministration to heal illness in ordinary Yharnam before darker consequences emerged.
Before the worst of the plague, Yharnam was an ordinary city of markets, trades, private devotion, and family life.

The Healing Church branded the Vile Bloods corruptors of sacred ministration and sent Logarius to destroy Cainhurst; unable to kill the immortal Queen Annalise, he sealed her in the throne room and guarded it the rest of his life.
Rom, once a Byrgenwerth scholar, was transformed by contact with a Great One and placed in the hidden lake by Willem to veil the blood moon and Queen Yharnam's secret.

Ludwig formalized Gehrman's small original workshop into the organized Healing Church Hunters, establishing ranks and theology, and later received the Holy Moonlight Sword through communion with the Great Ones.

The Healing Church Choir ran an orphanage ostensibly for plague orphans but actually used children as experimental subjects for ascension research; most died or went mad, and the few 'successes' became memoryless Celestial Emissaries.

Maria, a Cainhurst-descended but gifted student of Gehrman, wielded the Rakuyo (shared with her companion Simon) and was present at the fishing hamlet when scholars arrived, killed villagers, and desecrated the great one Kos.

In grief, Maria threw her Rakuyo into the hamlet's well and later spent her remaining years at the Research Hall seeking redemption through caring for patients, eventually dying there and being drawn into the Hunter's Nightmare.

Ludwig and other Church hunters eventually succumbed to the old blood they fought, with Ludwig transforming into a horse-fused beast, echoing a broader pattern of hunters falling to the forces they hunted.
Lawrence, founder of the Healing Church, became the very first cleric beast, completely and absolutely, beginning a recurring curse among Church clerics.

The Healing Church sealed and burned the entire district of Old Yharnam to contain the beast scourge, killing transformed and untransformed residents alike; the fire did not stop the plague's spread elsewhere.
Djura, who helped burn Old Yharnam, later returned to its ruins out of guilt to protect the remaining beasts from other hunters.
Amelia succeeded Lawrence as leader of the Healing Church, inheriting his pendant of authority, while the Church's hunters and clerics increasingly blurred healing with violence.

Gascoigne, partnered with the veteran hunter Henryk, lived with his wife Viola and their two daughters; she gave him a music box and he gave her a red-jeweled brooch, but as the hunt wore on he began losing his memories of them.
On the night the game's events begin, the player's hunter awakens in Iosefka's Clinic and receives a transfusion of old blood, beginning their own hunt.
Early in Central Yharnam, the player hears the distant screams of beasts and encounters the Cleric Beast, a long-suffering monster on the Great Bridge, establishing the scale of the city's horror.

That same night, Gascoigne failed to return home; Viola went searching for him without her music box and was later found dead near his transformation site, the circumstances of her death left ambiguous.

The player finds the transformed Gascoigne in the Tomb of Oedon, destroying corpses and warning of the inevitability of beasthood before fully succumbing; using the music box given by his daughter momentarily restores his humanity before he is defeated, seemingly asking forgiveness.
Returning Viola's brooch to Gascoigne's daughter prompts only the word 'mommy' before the window falls silent.

The player defeats the Blood-starved Beast in Old Yharnam, a creature twisted by exposure to ashen blood, and later confronts Vicar Amelia, who transforms into a beast mid-prayer, healing herself even after losing coherent thought.
The player defeats Rom the Vacuous Spider, causing the Blood Moon to rise permanently over Yharnam, revealing hidden Amygdalas and dramatically altering the city's enemies and world state.
Soon after, the player is abducted from Yharnam's streets by bell-ringing women serving the School of Mensis and taken to Yahar'gul.

In Yahar'gul, the player battles the One Reborn, a mass of fused bodies of Yharnam residents who received Church blood ministration before being abducted and processed by Mensis, healed and empowered during the fight by Chime Maidens.

The player enters the Nightmare of Mensis, a hellscape sustained by Micolash's broken mind and anchored to the presence of the infant Great One Mergo, who is never directly seen but only heard crying.
Defeating Mergo's Wet Nurse silences Mergo's crying, beginning the unraveling of the Mensis ritual's nightmare.

In events framed as occurring earlier in the timeline but explored later by the player, the Old Hunters' Hunter's Nightmare reveals Maria guarding the Astral Clock Tower leading to the fishing hamlet, her Rakuyo mysteriously restored, and her own guilt over failing to protect children, villagers, and patients surfacing when she is finally defeated.

Deeper in the Hunter's Nightmare, the player confronts the corpse of the great one Kos on the fishing hamlet shore and the Orphan of Kos, born violently from her body, wielding its own placenta before revealing ghostly wings in its final phase.
In the Grand Cathedral of the Hunter's Nightmare, Lawrence appears eternally burning as the first cleric beast, reaching toward his own real skull in recognition when it is brought near him.
After the Orphan of Kos is defeated, the Doll notes that Gehrman is finally sleeping soundly, suggesting the nightmare's grip on him has eased.
Back in the Hunter's Dream, Gehrman—who has guided roughly 300 hunters through the dream while tending graves—offers the player a final mercy: to end their dream with the Burial Blade.

If the player refuses Gehrman's offer, he rises to fight as the first hunter, reaching upward toward Maria's memory when finally defeated, bringing the confrontation full circle within the Hunter's Dream itself.

If the hunter has consumed enough Umbilical Cords to resist the call of Gehrman's mercy or his blade, the Moon Presence itself descends for a final battle, revealing its true relationship to the Hunter's Dream.

Depending on the player's choices, the game concludes in one of three distinct endings: death by Gehrman's blade, inheriting Gehrman's role in the dream, or becoming an infant Great One cradled by the Doll after defeating the Moon Presence.
